sources.entry: Roundup Issue Tracker - Simple-to-use and -install issue tracking system with command-line, web, REST, XML-RPC, and e-mail interfaces. Designed with flexibility in mind - not just another bug tracker. (Source Code) MIT/ZPL-2.0 Python/Docker

summary.name: Roundup Issue Tracker
summary.one_liner: Roundup is a Python-based, customizable issue-tracking system with command-line, web, REST, XML-RPC and e-mail interfaces.
use_cases: conference paper submission and referee management
summary.what_it_does: Roundup is an issue-tracking system written in Python that can be used through command-line, web, REST, XML-RPC and e-mail interfaces. It is based on a design by Ka-Ping Yee that won the Software Carpentry "Track" design competition. The page says it is highly customizable and can be set up for uses such as bug tracking, help desks, and lead tracking. The latest stable version listed is 2.6.0, which adds CSRF protection, reauthentication for sensitive field changes, and responsive updates to the classic UI. A bundled demo tracker can be started with a single command, and it can be installed with pip in a virtual environment or used to build a custom Docker image.
notable: Multiple interfaces: command-line, web, REST, XML-RPC and e-mail
Demo tracker runs without a full install (python demo.py or roundup-demo)
Installable with pip or usable to build a custom Docker image
Licensed MIT/ZPL-2.0 according to the awesome-selfhosted listing
caveats: Python 2 support ended with release 2.4.0 (July 2024); Python 3 is required for new trackers
Some 2.6.0 security fixes were still pending CVE or request approval at release time
